Harbour reopens after storm repairs

The fishing harbour reopened on Monday morning, three months after the autumn storm tore away a section of the breakwater and sank two moored boats. Crews worked through the winter to rebuild the wall with larger stone blocks.
Boats back in the harbour on Monday.
The town council said the repairs cost 2.4 million euros, most of it paid by the regional government. The council's budget had set aside a further sum for dredging the entrance channel, which silted up during the storm.
Fishermen welcomed the reopening but said the season had already been badly hit. "We lost the best weeks of the year," said the head of the fishermen's guild, who asked the council to bring forward the promised compensation payments.
The harbour master said boats would be guided in by a temporary light until the new beacon is installed next month, and asked skippers to keep to the marked channel in the meantime.
Work on the second phase, which raises the outer wall by a metre, is due to start in the spring and should be finished before the next storm season, according to the engineers in charge of the project.
